walkthroughs.body_html:
Themes in Economics — a core area of A-Level Economics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Themes in Economics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Themes in Economics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a shift in demand and a movement along the demand curve?
options: A change in price shifts the demand curve.
Demand always falls when supply increases.
A movement along the curve is caused by a change in price; a shift of the whole curve is caused by changes in other factors (income, tastes, substitute prices).
Automatic stabilisers are special government emergency funds.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between CPI and RPI as inflation measures?
options: Both measure price changes via a basket of goods, but RPI includes housing costs (mortgage interest) and uses an arithmetic mean; CPI excludes housing costs and uses a geometric mean — CPI is the official UK target measure.
CPI and RPI always give the same inflation figure.
CPI measures consumer prices and RPI measures retail prices — that's the only difference.
Demand always falls when supply increases.
CPI measures consumer prices and RPI measures retail prices — that's the only difference.
Automatic stabilisers are special government emergency funds.
Automatic stabilisers are interest rate changes by the central bank.

Features of the tax and benefit system that automatically cushion the economy without new legislation — e.g. unemployment benefits rise in slumps; tax revenues fall as incomes fall, supporting demand.
